newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF POSTS VICTORY IN FIRST MATCH AFTER LAYOFF.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF POSTS VICTORY IN FIRST MATCH AFTER LAYOFF.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf, playing for the first time in seven weeks, shook off the rust Thursday to beat American Amy Frazier 6-2 6-1 and advance to the quarter-finals of the WTA Advanta Championships.

The 27-year-old Graf, who decided to play in this event Sunday after previously announcing her withdrawal due to a chronic knee injury, saw room for improvement despite breaking Frazier's serve on each occasion in a 55-minute victory.
"I didn't serve as well as I wanted to," said Graf. "But I hadn't played a match in a long time, so I really shouldn't ask for more.
"As long as my knee didn't hurt I wasn't thinking about it. I was concentrating on my game."

Graf will face unseeded American Chanda Rubin in Friday's quarter-finals. Rubin needs to win this event to qualify for the last berth in next week's season-ending Chase Championships in New York. If Rubin falls short, Austrian Judith Wiesner will qualify.

Graf had thought her knee problem was related to an inflamation, but recently learned she had a slight tear in the tendon. Her treatment was changed and Graf says the knee has responded well, enabling her to play this week.

Graf stopped the flood of upsets that marked the tournament Wednesday, when all five seeds in action lost. Graf lashed out against the notion that some players were more concerned with preparing for next week than playing well here.
"If they felt that way they shouldn't enter in the first place," said defending champion Graf. "But I don't think any player wants to lose in the first round."

Two other seeds advanced Thursday, although number eight Barbara Paulus of Austria did not need to step on the court. Paulus advanced when American Zina Garrison-Jackson pulled out due to a shoulder injury.
Third seed Jana Novotna of the Czech Republic struggled before beating American Lori McNeil 6-4 7-5.
"Playing Lori, I know it's a race to see who's coming to the net," said Novotna. "I like to serve and volley. (But) I don't like to come in after every shot."
In another second-round match, Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia beat American Kimberly Po 6-4 6-4.
